LoRaWAN.definition: LoRaWAN is a low-power wide-area networking protocol designed to connect battery-operated devices to the internet through public, private or community networks.
LoRaWAN.deploymentFit: It is intended for IoT deployments that exchange relatively small amounts of data and need wide-area or difficult indoor coverage.
LoRaWAN.advantage: The standard is designed around range, device power use, network capacity and deployment cost.
LoRaWAN.limitation: A deployment still needs a suitable LoRaWAN network and the correct regional configuration; the catalogue label alone does not confirm those project details.

LTE CAT 1.definition: LTE Cat 1 is a 4G LTE device category first defined in 3GPP Release 8 and used by some IoT products.
LTE CAT 1.deploymentFit: It suits projects evaluating LTE cellular connectivity rather than the LPWA categories LTE-M or NB-IoT.
LTE CAT 1.advantage: It provides an LTE option for IoT products represented in this catalogue.
LTE CAT 1.limitation: LTE Cat 1 is not interchangeable with LTE-M or NB-IoT; buyers must confirm operator service and model requirements separately.
LTE CAT 1.sourceLabel: GSMA — Mobile IoT in a 5G Future

NB-IoT.definition: NB-IoT is a 3GPP-standardised cellular low-power wide-area technology that operates in licensed spectrum.
NB-IoT.deploymentFit: It is intended for IoT devices with low-throughput requirements, including deployments seeking extended rural or indoor coverage.
NB-IoT.advantage: The technology is designed for low device complexity, power efficiency and large numbers of connected devices.
NB-IoT.limitation: Network availability and supported features vary by mobile operator and deployment, so they must be checked for the project location.

LTE-M & NB-IoT.definition: LTE-M and NB-IoT are complementary cellular low-power wide-area radio technologies specified by 3GPP.
LTE-M & NB-IoT.deploymentFit: They address IoT deployments needing licensed-spectrum wide-area connectivity, with the appropriate choice depending on device and network requirements.
LTE-M & NB-IoT.advantage: Products listing both technologies give buyers two cellular LPWA options to evaluate against local network support.
LTE-M & NB-IoT.limitation: The catalogue field does not establish which modes, features or roaming arrangements are active on a specific operator network.

LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.definition: LTE-M and NB-IoT are complementary cellular low-power wide-area radio technologies specified by 3GPP.
LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.deploymentFit: This exact catalogue group combines those interface labels with a supplied data-bundle description; product records should be compared individually.
LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.advantage: Products in this group expose both cellular LPWA names in their source interface value.
LTE-M & NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.limitation: The label does not establish operator coverage, enabled features or fitness for a particular deployment.

NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.definition: NB-IoT is a 3GPP-standardised cellular low-power wide-area technology that operates in licensed spectrum.
NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.deploymentFit: This exact catalogue group combines NB-IoT with a supplied data-bundle description; buyers should compare each source record.
NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.advantage: NB-IoT is designed for low-throughput, low-complexity IoT devices and extended coverage scenarios.
NB-IoT, 10 years 500MB data.limitation: The label does not establish operator coverage, enabled features or fitness for a particular deployment.
